einzeiler: John J. Miller reflects on 370 episodes as The Great Books Podcast comes to an end.
kurzfassung: John J. Miller announces the final episode of The Great Books Podcast after a run of nearly eight years and 370 episodes. He looks back at the literature covered, the scholars who appeared as guests, and the staff who supported the production. Finally, he thanks his loyal audience and signs off with a famous quote from Hamlet.
stichpunkte: National Review discontinues The Great Books Podcast after 370 episodes.
The show started in 2017 as a weekly interview format about literature.
Shakespeare's Macbeth was the first covered book, and Goethe's The Sorrows of Young Werther was the last.
Miller intentionally never covered Hamlet, keeping it as an unfulfilled possibility.
Guests were the core of the show, given space to speak in paragraphs about their favorite works.
Production took place at Radio Free Hillsdale with technical and editorial support from colleagues.
Listeners are invited to follow future updates via heymiller.com and his book Reading Around.

clips.hook: Why Hamlet was intentionally left off the reading list
clips.text: The host purposely avoided covering Hamlet to maintain the comforting thought of having one more major literary work left to explore.

clips.hook: The honest truth about reading every book on the show
clips.text: Addressing a common inquiry, the speaker admits he has not personally read every single title discussed throughout the entire run.

clips.hook: Shifting the spotlight from host to guest
clips.text: While many interview shows center entirely around the personality leading the conversation, this production was intentionally designed to elevate invited experts.

clips.hook: The college radio station behind a national podcast
clips.text: Every single installment of the program was recorded inside the campus radio facilities of Hillsdale College.

beschreibung: John J. Miller brings the Great Books podcast to a close.
